dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] De-duplicate the `_positive_int` argparse converter shared by the bridge CLI and reconciler request parser into one location.
evidence: _bridge_commands.py:101-109 `def _positive_int(value: str) -> int:` raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be a positive integer")`
request.py:26-33 defines the same `_positive_int` with identical body and message
dropped.finding: The `_positive_int` argparse converter is duplicated verbatim in both `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py`, with identical logic and error message; the two can drift independently.
scenarios: A future change to the ceiling-validation rule (e.g. an upper bound) updated in one module but not the other yields inconsistent CLI vs engine validation.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm exit 2 (hard failure) is the intended classification for SelectionStaleError vs a reschedule, and document/test the operator-facing consequence for concurrent deletion.
evidence: reconcile_helpers.py:378-384 `ensure_selection_current` raises `SelectionStaleError` when a preflight target is absent at locked load

ADR 0092 documents fail-closed: 'A partially unresolved or subsequently vanished selection fails closed without differ or apply.' — so exit 2 is intended, but conflates a transient race with a caller error
dropped.finding: A canonical selection that resolves at preflight but vanishes before the under-lock load raises `SelectionStaleError`, which `run_pass` maps to exit 2 (hard error) — the same code as an invalid invocation — rather than the reschedule/benign exit used for other under-lock races; a concurrent ticket deletion will therefore fail the scheduled job.
scenarios: Operator runs `bridge sync --only FOO`; FOO is deleted by another writer between preflight resolution and the locked load — the workflow step exits 2 and fails the job instead of rescheduling.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the bootstrap-strict/bootstrap-throttle → `bridge sync --max-changes N` (Mode.LIVE) remap is intended to be phase-gated as LIVE, and document the gate-interaction change for operators relying on bootstrap-level gates.
evidence: reconcile-bridge.yml:267-268 `bootstrap-strict) command=(rebar bridge sync --max-changes 10)` / `bootstrap-throttle) command=(rebar bridge sync --max-changes 100)`
request.py:108-109 `elif args.command == "sync": target_mode = mode_mod.Mode.LIVE` — sync always normalizes to LIVE regardless of --max-changes
mode.py:133-138 MODE_CAPS shows BOOTSTRAP_STRICT=10 / BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE=100 were distinct Mode members below LIVE
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py:141-142 confirms a throttle-level gate blocks a higher mode but permits equal/lower — LIVE now trips it where BOOTSTRAP would not
dropped.finding: Workflow rollout profiles `bootstrap-strict`/`bootstrap-throttle` are remapped from the dedicated `Mode.BOOTSTRAP_STRICT`/`Mode.BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (rank below LIVE) to `rebar bridge sync --max-changes N`, which normalizes to `Mode.LIVE`. Because `check_phase_gate` blocks iff `target_mode > gated_mode`, a phase gate set to a bootstrap level that previously PERMITTED a bootstrap-throttle pass will now BLOCK it, since LIVE outranks the bootstrap modes. This is a silent operational-behavior change for anyone dispatching those workflow profiles while a rollout gate is set.
scenarios: Operator dispatches the workflow with mode=bootstrap-throttle while a phase gate is pinned at bootstrap level during a staged rollout; the pass is now gated/blocked where it previously proceeded.
